The Parametric Bootstrap of a Prediction Interval

Source: R/predict_bootstrap.R
predictive_bootstrap.Rd

Returns the components of the predictive mixture that predictive_response() reads for pred_bootstrap(). There is one component per replica, which is the fit refitted on a response simulated from the fitted model and read at the rows predicted with no estimation uncertainty of its own.

Usage

predictive_bootstrap(object, spec, design, aside, n_boot, refit)

Arguments

object

The StatmodFit().

spec, design

The specification and design at the rows predicted, in which the columns of the effects set aside are zero.

aside

The rows of random_modes() that are not "conditional".

n_boot

The number of replicas, from pred_bootstrap().

refit

"coefficients" or "full".

Value

A list of components, each a list with eta, C and weight. The list has the attribute infinite_variance, which is TRUE where a prior has no variance. The weights of the components add up to one.

Details

A replica draws the response from the family at the fitted model. The effects of a modelterms7::random() term that random sets aside are drawn afresh from the prior that the fit estimated, so the groups of the data are new groups in every replica, as they are in the sampling distribution of the population-level estimates on which a new group's prediction rests. The effects of a term read "conditional" keep their estimates: the prediction is about those groups, and their effects are the quantity predicted rather than a source of variation. Every other coefficient keeps its estimate. The replica is then refitted in one of two ways:

"coefficients"

every coefficient is re-estimated at the hyperparameters that the fit reached. A coefficient that the fit estimated on its criterion (a dispersion under reml()) is estimated there again while the hyperparameters are held, so the replica's estimator is the fit's.

"full"

the hyperparameters are chosen again by the fit's own criteria, so their uncertainty enters the interval too, and the path of a kinked penalty is walked again, warm started from the fit's coefficients. A cross-validated criterion needs the data's folds and is rejected.

Every refit starts at the optimum that the fit found: its coefficients, including those that the fit estimated on its criterion, and its hyperparameters. The bootstrap is rejected for a model with a block that moves with its coefficients (modelterms7::seg(), modelterms7::jump(), modelterms7::jseg(), modelterms7::nl()) and for a response that is not one number per observation.

Each replica gives the component \((\hat\eta^*_b, C^*_b)\): its predictors at the rows predicted and the covariance that the effects set aside add, at its own hyperparameters. The interval is the mixture's, which is the parametric bootstrap predictive distribution of Harris (1989); the default pred_averaged() is its normal approximation, in which the sampling distribution of the estimates is replaced by \(\mathrm{N}(\hat \beta, \widehat{V})\). A replica whose refit fails is left out, and the warning reports how many were.

References

Harris, I. R. (1989). Predictive fit for natural exponential families. Biometrika, 76, 675–684.

See also

predict.StatmodFit(), the caller, predictive_response() for the mixture.

Examples

set.seed(2)
dd <- data.frame(x = runif(30))
dd$y <- 1 + dd$x + rnorm(30, sd = 0.5)
fit <- statmod(y ~ x, distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), dd)
predict(fit, what = "response", newdata = data.frame(x = 0.5),
        interval = prediction_interval(
          predictive = pred_bootstrap(n = 20)))
#>        fit        se     lower    upper
#> 1 1.547902 0.5891418 0.3767825 2.695134
